rumours: Caravanners in Ebonheart whisper that forged customs matrices have been turning up in crates across the Stonefalls Inner Sea District.
Watchmen along the Stonefalls ash-tracks say blue ancestor-lanterns have been seen flickering inside old Velothi tombs after midnight.
Retainers serving Grand Council Legate Varro and Councilor Brara Morvayn posted fresh House writs at Ebonheart for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of Stonefalls swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.
Guild clerks in Ebonheart complain that sealed amphorae marked with a red-wax bell bypass the harbour-watch without inspection.
Herders and muck-farmers in the Stonefalls Inner Sea District still leave a strip of cured scrib-jerky on the threshold stones to appease the hearth-ancestors.
An archivist from Vivec's Library arrived in Ebonheart last week asking after First Council Dwemer valve-charts.
Apothecaries in Ebonheart pay good drakes for luminous Russula and Bungler's Bane scraped from the damp grottoes of Stonefalls.
Buoyant Armigers drinking in Ebonheart still argue over which House company held the foyada pass during the last Blight surge.
Smugglers working the coves and lava-tubes of Stonefalls use chipped Daedric runes to mark their midnight drop-sites.

legends: In the First Era, before the Battle of Red Mountain, the Chimeri prophet Veloth blessed the boundary-cairns of Stonefalls so that no ancestor's name would be lost to the ash.
Old ballads of Ebonheart tell of an Indoril banner-bearer who sealed his company's reliquary beneath a stronghold in Stonefalls and swore his ghost would guard the lintel until the Tribunal's return.

Folk in the Stonefalls Inner Sea District speak of the Ashen Pilgrim, a silent figure in woven chitin who walks the foyadas of Stonefalls during dusk-storms, relighting extinguished shrine-lamps with a single coal.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Ebonheart, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of Stonefalls.
During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Stonefalls Inner Sea District stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Ebonheart for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Ebonheart
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Ebonheart,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the Stonefalls passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Stonefalls Inner Sea District
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Stonefalls Inner Sea District tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Ebonheart keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of Stonefalls
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Ebonheart with glass at your side,
For the spirits of Stonefalls in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the Stonefalls Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of Stonefalls over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Ebonheart alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

rumours: Caravanners in Mournhold whisper that forged customs matrices have been turning up in crates across the Sacred Precincts of Deshaan.
Watchmen along the Deshaan ash-tracks say blue ancestor-lanterns have been seen flickering inside old Velothi tombs after midnight.
Retainers serving King Hlaalu Helseth and Archcanon Gavas Drin posted fresh House writs at Mournhold for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of Deshaan swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.
Guild clerks in Mournhold complain that sealed amphorae marked with a red-wax bell bypass the harbour-watch without inspection.
Herders and muck-farmers in the Sacred Precincts of Deshaan still leave a strip of cured scrib-jerky on the threshold stones to appease the hearth-ancestors.
An archivist from Vivec's Library arrived in Mournhold last week asking after First Council Dwemer valve-charts.
Apothecaries in Mournhold pay good drakes for luminous Russula and Bungler's Bane scraped from the damp grottoes of Deshaan.
Buoyant Armigers drinking in Mournhold still argue over which House company held the foyada pass during the last Blight surge.
Smugglers working the coves and lava-tubes of Deshaan use chipped Daedric runes to mark their midnight drop-sites.

legends: In the First Era, before the Battle of Red Mountain, the Chimeri prophet Veloth blessed the boundary-cairns of Deshaan so that no ancestor's name would be lost to the ash.
Old ballads of Mournhold tell of an Indoril banner-bearer who sealed his company's reliquary beneath a stronghold in Deshaan and swore his ghost would guard the lintel until the Tribunal's return.

Folk in the Sacred Precincts of Deshaan speak of the Ashen Pilgrim, a silent figure in woven chitin who walks the foyadas of Deshaan during dusk-storms, relighting extinguished shrine-lamps with a single coal.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Mournhold, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of Deshaan.
During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Sacred Precincts of Deshaan stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Mournhold for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Mournhold
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Mournhold,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the Deshaan passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Sacred Precincts of Deshaan
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Sacred Precincts of Deshaan tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Mournhold keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of Deshaan
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Mournhold with glass at your side,
For the spirits of Deshaan in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the Deshaan Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of Deshaan over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Mournhold alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

rumours: Caravanners in Necrom whisper that forged customs matrices have been turning up in crates across the Ossuary Marches of Molag Amur.
Watchmen along the Molag Amur ash-tracks say blue ancestor-lanterns have been seen flickering inside old Velothi tombs after midnight.
Retainers serving Keeper-Prelate Faram Indoril of the Dead posted fresh House writs at Necrom for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of Molag Amur swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.
Guild clerks in Necrom complain that sealed amphorae marked with a red-wax bell bypass the harbour-watch without inspection.
Herders and muck-farmers in the Ossuary Marches of Molag Amur still leave a strip of cured scrib-jerky on the threshold stones to appease the hearth-ancestors.
An archivist from Vivec's Library arrived in Necrom last week asking after First Council Dwemer valve-charts.
Apothecaries in Necrom pay good drakes for luminous Russula and Bungler's Bane scraped from the damp grottoes of Molag Amur.
Buoyant Armigers drinking in Necrom still argue over which House company held the foyada pass during the last Blight surge.
Smugglers working the coves and lava-tubes of Molag Amur use chipped Daedric runes to mark their midnight drop-sites.

legends: In the First Era, before the Battle of Red Mountain, the Chimeri prophet Veloth blessed the boundary-cairns of Molag Amur so that no ancestor's name would be lost to the ash.
Old ballads of Necrom tell of an Indoril banner-bearer who sealed his company's reliquary beneath a stronghold in Molag Amur and swore his ghost would guard the lintel until the Tribunal's return.

Folk in the Ossuary Marches of Molag Amur speak of the Ashen Pilgrim, a silent figure in woven chitin who walks the foyadas of Molag Amur during dusk-storms, relighting extinguished shrine-lamps with a single coal.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Necrom, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of Molag Amur.
During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Ossuary Marches of Molag Amur stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Necrom for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Necrom
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Necrom,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the Molag Amur passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Ossuary Marches of Molag Amur
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Ossuary Marches of Molag Amur tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Necrom keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of Molag Amur
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Necrom with glass at your side,
For the spirits of Molag Amur in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the Molag Amur Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of Molag Amur over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Necrom alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

rumours: Caravanners in Sadrith Mora whisper that forged customs matrices have been turning up in crates across the Mushroom Isles of Telvannis.
Watchmen along the Telvannis ash-tracks say blue ancestor-lanterns have been seen flickering inside old Velothi tombs after midnight.
Retainers serving Master Aryon and the Council of Tel Naga posted fresh House writs at Sadrith Mora for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of Telvannis swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.
Guild clerks in Sadrith Mora complain that sealed amphorae marked with a red-wax bell bypass the harbour-watch without inspection.
Herders and muck-farmers in the Mushroom Isles of Telvannis still leave a strip of cured scrib-jerky on the threshold stones to appease the hearth-ancestors.
An archivist from Vivec's Library arrived in Sadrith Mora last week asking after First Council Dwemer valve-charts.
Apothecaries in Sadrith Mora pay good drakes for luminous Russula and Bungler's Bane scraped from the damp grottoes of Telvannis.
Buoyant Armigers drinking in Sadrith Mora still argue over which House company held the foyada pass during the last Blight surge.
Smugglers working the coves and lava-tubes of Telvannis use chipped Daedric runes to mark their midnight drop-sites.

legends: In the First Era, before the Battle of Red Mountain, the Chimeri prophet Veloth blessed the boundary-cairns of Telvannis so that no ancestor's name would be lost to the ash.

Old ballads of Sadrith Mora tell of an Indoril banner-bearer who sealed his company's reliquary beneath a stronghold in Telvannis and swore his ghost would guard the lintel until the Tribunal's return.

Folk in the Mushroom Isles of Telvannis speak of the Ashen Pilgrim, a silent figure in woven chitin who walks the foyadas of Telvannis during dusk-storms, relighting extinguished shrine-lamps with a single coal.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Sadrith Mora, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of Telvannis.

During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Mushroom Isles of Telvannis stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Sadrith Mora for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Sadrith Mora
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Sadrith Mora,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the Telvannis passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Mushroom Isles of Telvannis
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Mushroom Isles of Telvannis tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Sadrith Mora keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of Telvannis
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Sadrith Mora with glass at your side,
For the spirits of Telvannis in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the Telvannis Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of Telvannis over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Sadrith Mora alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

rumours: Caravanners in Dagon Fel whisper that forged customs matrices have been turning up in crates across the Basalt Archipelago of Sheogorad.
Watchmen along the Sheogorad ash-tracks say blue ancestor-lanterns have been seen flickering inside old Velothi tombs after midnight.
Retainers serving Reeve Hrolfdir and Prior Ralden of Sanctus Shrine posted fresh House writs at Dagon Fel for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of Sheogorad swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.

legends: In the First Era, before the Battle of Red Mountain, the Chimeri prophet Veloth blessed the boundary-cairns of Sheogorad so that no ancestor's name would be lost to the ash.
Old ballads of Dagon Fel tell of an Indoril banner-bearer who sealed his company's reliquary beneath a stronghold in Sheogorad and swore his ghost would guard the lintel until the Tribunal's return.

Folk in the Basalt Archipelago of Sheogorad speak of the Ashen Pilgrim, a silent figure in woven chitin who walks the foyadas of Sheogorad during dusk-storms, relighting extinguished shrine-lamps with a single coal.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Dagon Fel, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of Sheogorad.

During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Basalt Archipelago of Sheogorad stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Dagon Fel for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Dagon Fel
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Dagon Fel,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the Sheogorad passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Basalt Archipelago of Sheogorad
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Basalt Archipelago of Sheogorad tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Dagon Fel keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of Sheogorad
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Dagon Fel with glass at your side,
For the spirits of Sheogorad in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the Sheogorad Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of Sheogorad over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Dagon Fel alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

Beneath the oldest foundations of Ald'ruhn, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of the Vvardenfell Ashlands.

During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Redoran Council Seat of the Ashlands stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Ald'ruhn for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Ald'ruhn
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Ald'ruhn,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the the Vvardenfell Ashlands passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Redoran Council Seat of the Ashlands
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Redoran Council Seat of the Ashlands tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Ald'ruhn keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of the Vvardenfell Ashlands
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Ald'ruhn with glass at your side,
For the spirits of the Vvardenfell Ashlands in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the the Vvardenfell Ashlands Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of the Vvardenfell Ashlands over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Ald'ruhn alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

rumours: Caravanners in Vos whisper that forged customs matrices have been turning up in crates across the Golden Savannah of the Grazelands.
Watchmen along the the Grazelands ash-tracks say blue ancestor-lanterns have been seen flickering inside old Velothi tombs after midnight.
Retainers serving Master Aryon of Tel Vos and Ashkhan Kaushad of the Zainab posted fresh House writs at Vos for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of the Grazelands swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.
Guild clerks in Vos complain that sealed amphorae marked with a red-wax bell bypass the harbour-watch without inspection.
Herders and muck-farmers in the Golden Savannah of the Grazelands still leave a strip of cured scrib-jerky on the threshold stones to appease the hearth-ancestors.
An archivist from Vivec's Library arrived in Vos last week asking after First Council Dwemer valve-charts.
Apothecaries in Vos pay good drakes for luminous Russula and Bungler's Bane scraped from the damp grottoes of the Grazelands.
Buoyant Armigers drinking in Vos still argue over which House company held the foyada pass during the last Blight surge.
Smugglers working the coves and lava-tubes of the Grazelands use chipped Daedric runes to mark their midnight drop-sites.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Vos
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Vos,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the the Grazelands passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Golden Savannah of the Grazelands
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Golden Savannah of the Grazelands tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Vos keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of the Grazelands
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Vos with glass at your side,
For the spirits of the Grazelands in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the the Grazelands Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of the Grazelands over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Vos alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

Retainers serving Buoyant Armiger Commander Traven Marvos and Master Gilvas Barelo posted fresh House writs at Molag Mar for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of Azura's Coast swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.

Herders and muck-farmers in the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast still leave a strip of cured scrib-jerky on the threshold stones to appease the hearth-ancestors.
An archivist from Vivec's Library arrived in Molag Mar last week asking after First Council Dwemer valve-charts.
Apothecaries in Molag Mar pay good drakes for luminous Russula and Bungler's Bane scraped from the damp grottoes of Azura's Coast.
Buoyant Armigers drinking in Molag Mar still argue over which House company held the foyada pass during the last Blight surge.
Smugglers working the coves and lava-tubes of Azura's Coast use chipped Daedric runes to mark their midnight drop-sites.

lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast tonight,

For the spirits of Azura's Coast in silence abide.

rumours: Caravanners in Balmora whisper that forged customs matrices have been turning up in crates across the Hlaalu Trade District of the West Gash.
Watchmen along the the West Gash ash-tracks say blue ancestor-lanterns have been seen flickering inside old Velothi tombs after midnight.
Retainers serving Councilor Nileno Dorvayn and Governor-Magistrate of Caldera posted fresh House writs at Balmora for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of the West Gash swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.
Guild clerks in Balmora complain that sealed amphorae marked with a red-wax bell bypass the harbour-watch without inspection.
Herders and muck-farmers in the Hlaalu Trade District of the West Gash still leave a strip of cured scrib-jerky on the threshold stones to appease the hearth-ancestors.
An archivist from Vivec's Library arrived in Balmora last week asking after First Council Dwemer valve-charts.
Apothecaries in Balmora pay good drakes for luminous Russula and Bungler's Bane scraped from the damp grottoes of the West Gash.
Buoyant Armigers drinking in Balmora still argue over which House company held the foyada pass during the last Blight surge.
Smugglers working the coves and lava-tubes of the West Gash use chipped Daedric runes to mark their midnight drop-sites.

legends: In the First Era, before the Battle of Red Mountain, the Chimeri prophet Veloth blessed the boundary-cairns of the West Gash so that no ancestor's name would be lost to the ash.

Old ballads of Balmora tell of an Indoril banner-bearer who sealed his company's reliquary beneath a stronghold in the West Gash and swore his ghost would guard the lintel until the Tribunal's return.

Folk in the Hlaalu Trade District of the West Gash speak of the Ashen Pilgrim, a silent figure in woven chitin who walks the foyadas of the West Gash during dusk-storms, relighting extinguished shrine-lamps with a single coal.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Balmora, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of the West Gash.

During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Hlaalu Trade District of the West Gash stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Balmora for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

legends: In the First Era, before the Battle of Red Mountain, the Chimeri prophet Veloth blessed the boundary-cairns of the Bitter Coast so that no ancestor's name would be lost to the ash.

Old ballads of Gnaar Mok tell of an Indoril banner-bearer who sealed his company's reliquary beneath a stronghold in the Bitter Coast and swore his ghost would guard the lintel until the Tribunal's return.

Folk in the Mangrove Marshes of the Bitter Coast speak of the Ashen Pilgrim, a silent figure in woven chitin who walks the foyadas of the Bitter Coast during dusk-storms, relighting extinguished shrine-lamps with a single coal.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Gnaar Mok, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of the Bitter Coast.

During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Mangrove Marshes of the Bitter Coast stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Gnaar Mok for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Gnaar Mok
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Gnaar Mok,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the the Bitter Coast passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Mangrove Marshes of the Bitter Coast
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Mangrove Marshes of the Bitter Coast tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Gnaar Mok keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of the Bitter Coast
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Gnaar Mok with glass at your side,
For the spirits of the Bitter Coast in silence abide.

lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of the Bitter Coast over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Gnaar Mok alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

legends: In the First Era, before the Battle of Red Mountain, the Chimeri prophet Veloth blessed the boundary-cairns of the Ascadian Isles so that no ancestor's name would be lost to the ash.

Old ballads of Vivec City tell of an Indoril banner-bearer who sealed his company's reliquary beneath a stronghold in the Ascadian Isles and swore his ghost would guard the lintel until the Tribunal's return.

Folk in the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles speak of the Ashen Pilgrim, a silent figure in woven chitin who walks the foyadas of the Ascadian Isles during dusk-storms, relighting extinguished shrine-lamps with a single coal.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Vivec City, Dwemer steam-conduits still carry warm geothermal breath from the deep magma-chambers of the Ascadian Isles.

During the Four-Score War, a House retainer of the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles stood alone on the basalt bridge outside Vivec City for three days, holding back an invading cohort with a glass spear.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Vivec City
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Vivec City,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the the Ascadian Isles passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Vivec City keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of the Ascadian Isles
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Vivec City with glass at your side,
For the spirits of the Ascadian Isles in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the the Ascadian Isles Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of the Ascadian Isles over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Vivec City alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

rumours: Caravanners in Ghostgate whisper that forged customs matrices have been turning up in crates across the Blighted Cordon of Red Mountain.
Watchmen along the Red Mountain ash-tracks say blue ancestor-lanterns have been seen flickering inside old Velothi tombs after midnight.
Retainers serving Knight-Commander Ralyn Othravel of the Ghostgate Towers posted fresh House writs at Ghostgate for anyone who can clear the blighted mine-galleries.
Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of Red Mountain swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.
Guild clerks in Ghostgate complain that sealed amphorae marked with a red-wax bell bypass the harbour-watch without inspection.
Herders and muck-farmers in the Blighted Cordon of Red Mountain still leave a strip of cured scrib-jerky on the threshold stones to appease the hearth-ancestors.
An archivist from Vivec's Library arrived in Ghostgate last week asking after First Council Dwemer valve-charts.
Apothecaries in Ghostgate pay good drakes for luminous Russula and Bungler's Bane scraped from the damp grottoes of Red Mountain.
Buoyant Armigers drinking in Ghostgate still argue over which House company held the foyada pass during the last Blight surge.
Smugglers working the coves and lava-tubes of Red Mountain use chipped Daedric runes to mark their midnight drop-sites.

songs.title: The Ash-Lantern Road to Ghostgate
lines: O wrap your scarf tight on the road to Ghostgate,
Where the silt-striders call through the cinder and rain;
Keep the ancestor-lamp burning steady and clear,
Through the Red Mountain passes til hearth-fires appear.

songs.title: Watchfires of the Blighted Cordon of Red Mountain
lines: Raise a cup of warm mazte for the Blighted Cordon of Red Mountain tonight,
Where the bug-lamps of chitin glow amber and bright;
Though the Councillors scheme and the ash-tempests blow,
Still the folk of Ghostgate keep the old oaths below.

songs.title: Cairns of Red Mountain
lines: From the sea-grottoes up to the foyada crest,
Where the bones of the clan in their ash-niches rest;
Count the leagues into Ghostgate with glass at your side,
For the spirits of Red Mountain in silence abide.

songs.title: Canticle of the Red Mountain Way-Cairn 1
lines: By basalt and mushroom past cairn 1 we stride,
Where the winds of Red Mountain over ash-valleys ride;
Keep the hearth-coal of Ghostgate alight in the storm,
Where the ancestor-wards keep the caravan warm.

Pilgrims at the roadside shrines of Solstheim swear the stone trioliths hum softly whenever an ash-storm rolls down from the caldera.

abasipal_wharf.hook: Abasipal Wharf (village) stands at (3367, -943) in Stonefalls, where the weathered stone and chitin of the Stonefalls Inner Sea District still bear the marks of Ebonheart's House and Temple history.
abasipal_wharf.rumour: Travellers in Ebonheart say anyone who searches Abasipal Wharf in Stonefalls will find traces of the old Velothi wardens and recent smugglers' caches.

notes.title: Surveyor's Ash-Log at Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Vivec Geographical & Propylon Society
pages: On the fourteenth day of our circuit through the Stonefalls Inner Sea District, we set our brass transit-rod at Abasipal Wharf (survey grid 3367, -943 in Stonefalls). The basalt and chitin foundations here show three distinct strata beneath the volcanic ash, and our Dunmer guide from Ebonheart insisted on leaving a pinch of bonemeal at the threshold before sundown.

notes.title: House Watch Dispatch: Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Chancery of Ebonheart
pages: To the watch-retainer posted at Abasipal Wharf (3367, -943): by warrant of Grand Council Legate Varro and Councilor Brara Morvayn in Ebonheart, patrols along this sector of Stonefalls are to inspect all night-caravans bearing unsealed ebony or flin crates. Any bearer carrying a red-wax Sixth House chime is to be detained and escorted to Ebonheart at once.

notes.title: Factor's Private Missive from Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Factor-Clerk Llaren
pages: My dear colleague in Ebonheart: the inventory stored at Abasipal Wharf (grid 3367, -943 in the Stonefalls Inner Sea District) remains untouched by the excise bailiffs. So long as Stonefalls stays distracted by council rivalries, our pack-guars can move two dozen amphorae a week past Abasipal Wharf without paying a single drake in tariff.

notes.title: Antiquarian Notes on Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Curator Mehra of the Hall of Wisdom
pages: Among the secondary sites of Stonefalls, Abasipal Wharf (situated at coordinates 3367, -943 within the Stonefalls Inner Sea District) merits closer study by the Temple archivists. The lintel joints preserve tool-marks characteristic of early Velothi masonry, yet the lower drainage follows an older Dwemer alignment oriented toward Ebonheart.

notes.title: Caravanner's Chalk-Warning at Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Silt-Strider Guide of Ebonheart
pages: Travellers bound for Ebonheart across Stonefalls: do not tether your pack-guars at Abasipal Wharf (3367, -943) when the ash-fog thickens at dusk. Three kagouti-hunters and a House outrider vanished near the outer stones of Abasipal Wharf last fortnight, and the watch in the Stonefalls Inner Sea District has not yet purged the interior.

notes.title: Rubbing from the Velothi Lintel at Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Temple Chronicler of Ebonheart
pages: Transcribed from the ash-scoured lintel at Abasipal Wharf (3367, -943 in the Stonefalls Inner Sea District): 'Here stood the third hearth-watch of the Stonefalls march, consecrated by the clan-elders on the high road to Ebonheart. Let him who takes shelter within these stones keep the ancestor-coal lit and the threshold clean.'

notes.title: Tithe and Assay Roll of Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Factor-Steward of Ebonheart
pages: Extracted from the district assessment book for Abasipal Wharf (grid 3367, -943 in Stonefalls): twelve bales of salted trama-root, four casks of sujamma, and eighteen ebony drakes remitted to the the Stonefalls Inner Sea District wardens at Ebonheart, with arrears noted since the latest ash-storms.

notes.title: Outrider's Night-Watch Report: Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Scout-Retainer of Ebonheart
pages: Submitted to the guard-captain at Ebonheart: at midnight we observed amber chitin-lanterns signaling from the upper ridge of Abasipal Wharf (3367, -943 in Stonefalls). Fresh guar-tracks lead from the postern toward the coast, matching the smuggling ring hunted across the Stonefalls Inner Sea District.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Ash-Slip Left at Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Wayfarer of the Seven Graces
pages: Tucked beneath a weathered cairn-stone at Abasipal Wharf (3367, -943 in Stonefalls): 'By courtesy, mercy, and valor, may the Three and our honoured ancestors watch over those who walk from Abasipal Wharf to Ebonheart through the ash of the Stonefalls Inner Sea District.'

notes.title: Pack-Guar Cargo Tally: Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Caravan Master of Ebonheart
pages: Waybill recovered from a waxing-crate at Abasipal Wharf (3367, -943 in the Stonefalls Inner Sea District): six jars of refined scuttle, two bolts of boiled netch-leather, and one sealed brass tube addressed to the council clerk in Ebonheart across Stonefalls.

notes.title: Boundary-Writ of Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Council Archivist of Ebonheart
pages: Recorded in the House cadastre for Abasipal Wharf (3367, -943 in Stonefalls): all salvage, spore-rights, and ancestral niche-keys within Abasipal Wharf remain subject to the custom of the Stonefalls Inner Sea District and the magistrate's seal at Ebonheart.

notes.title: Armiger Courier Slip at Abasipal Wharf
notes.author: Patrol-Signaler of Ebonheart
pages: Left in the bronze message-cylinder at Abasipal Wharf (3367, -943): the ash-wind over Stonefalls has shifted east; all riders bound for Ebonheart in the Stonefalls Inner Sea District should check the ward-lanterns at Abasipal Wharf before pressing on.

notes.title: Antiquarian Notes on Azeanabi Ruins

notes.title: Caravanner's Chalk-Warning at Azeanabi Ruins
notes.author: Silt-Strider Guide of Sadrith Mora

notes.title: Tithe and Assay Roll of Azeanabi Ruins
notes.author: Factor-Steward of Sadrith Mora

notes.title: Outrider's Night-Watch Report: Azeanabi Ruins
notes.author: Scout-Retainer of Sadrith Mora
pages: Submitted to the guard-captain at Sadrith Mora: at midnight we observed amber chitin-lanterns signaling from the upper ridge of Azeanabi Ruins (9914, -81 in Telvannis). Fresh guar-tracks lead from the postern toward the coast, matching the smuggling ring hunted across the Mushroom Isles of Telvannis.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Ash-Slip Left at Azeanabi Ruins

notes.author: Caravan Master of Sadrith Mora

notes.author: Council Archivist of Sadrith Mora

pages: Travellers bound for Ald'ruhn across the Vvardenfell Ashlands: do not tether your pack-guars at Yesamsi (5422, -1392) when the ash-fog thickens at dusk. Three kagouti-hunters and a House outrider vanished near the outer stones of Yesamsi last fortnight, and the watch in the Redoran Council Seat of the Ashlands has not yet purged the interior.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Ash-Slip Left at Yesamsi

pages: On the fourteenth day of our circuit through the Golden Savannah of the Grazelands, we set our brass transit-rod at Raviro Ancestral Tomb (survey grid 8096, -1570 in the Grazelands). The basalt and chitin foundations here show three distinct strata beneath the volcanic ash, and our Dunmer guide from Vos insisted on leaving a pinch of bonemeal at the threshold before sundown.

notes.title: Factor's Private Missive from Raviro Ancestral Tomb
notes.author: Factor-Clerk Llaren
pages: My dear colleague in Vos: the inventory stored at Raviro Ancestral Tomb (grid 8096, -1570 in the Golden Savannah of the Grazelands) remains untouched by the excise bailiffs. So long as the Grazelands stays distracted by council rivalries, our pack-guars can move two dozen amphorae a week past Raviro Ancestral Tomb without paying a single drake in tariff.

notes.title: Caravanner's Chalk-Warning at Raviro Ancestral Tomb

notes.author: Scout-Retainer of Vos

pages: On the fourteenth day of our circuit through the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast, we set our brass transit-rod at Ancient Shipwreck (survey grid 8584, 664 in Azura's Coast). The basalt and chitin foundations here show three distinct strata beneath the volcanic ash, and our Dunmer guide from Molag Mar insisted on leaving a pinch of bonemeal at the threshold before sundown.

notes.title: House Watch Dispatch: Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Chancery of Molag Mar
pages: To the watch-retainer posted at Ancient Shipwreck (8584, 664): by warrant of Buoyant Armiger Commander Traven Marvos and Master Gilvas Barelo in Molag Mar, patrols along this sector of Azura's Coast are to inspect all night-caravans bearing unsealed ebony or flin crates. Any bearer carrying a red-wax Sixth House chime is to be detained and escorted to Molag Mar at once.

notes.title: Factor's Private Missive from Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Factor-Clerk Llaren
pages: My dear colleague in Molag Mar: the inventory stored at Ancient Shipwreck (grid 8584, 664 in the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast) remains untouched by the excise bailiffs. So long as Azura's Coast stays distracted by council rivalries, our pack-guars can move two dozen amphorae a week past Ancient Shipwreck without paying a single drake in tariff.

notes.title: Antiquarian Notes on Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Curator Mehra of the Hall of Wisdom
pages: Among the secondary sites of Azura's Coast, Ancient Shipwreck (situated at coordinates 8584, 664 within the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast) merits closer study by the Temple archivists. The lintel joints preserve tool-marks characteristic of early Velothi masonry, yet the lower drainage follows an older Dwemer alignment oriented toward Molag Mar.

notes.title: Caravanner's Chalk-Warning at Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Silt-Strider Guide of Molag Mar
pages: Travellers bound for Molag Mar across Azura's Coast: do not tether your pack-guars at Ancient Shipwreck (8584, 664) when the ash-fog thickens at dusk. Three kagouti-hunters and a House outrider vanished near the outer stones of Ancient Shipwreck last fortnight, and the watch in the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast has not yet purged the interior.

notes.title: Rubbing from the Velothi Lintel at Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Temple Chronicler of Molag Mar
pages: Transcribed from the ash-scoured lintel at Ancient Shipwreck (8584, 664 in the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast): 'Here stood the third hearth-watch of the Azura's Coast march, consecrated by the clan-elders on the high road to Molag Mar. Let him who takes shelter within these stones keep the ancestor-coal lit and the threshold clean.'

notes.title: Tithe and Assay Roll of Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Factor-Steward of Molag Mar
pages: Extracted from the district assessment book for Ancient Shipwreck (grid 8584, 664 in Azura's Coast): twelve bales of salted trama-root, four casks of sujamma, and eighteen ebony drakes remitted to the the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast wardens at Molag Mar, with arrears noted since the latest ash-storms.

notes.title: Outrider's Night-Watch Report: Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Scout-Retainer of Molag Mar
pages: Submitted to the guard-captain at Molag Mar: at midnight we observed amber chitin-lanterns signaling from the upper ridge of Ancient Shipwreck (8584, 664 in Azura's Coast). Fresh guar-tracks lead from the postern toward the coast, matching the smuggling ring hunted across the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Ash-Slip Left at Ancient Shipwreck

pages: Tucked beneath a weathered cairn-stone at Ancient Shipwreck (8584, 664 in Azura's Coast): 'By courtesy, mercy, and valor, may the Three and our honoured ancestors watch over those who walk from Ancient Shipwreck to Molag Mar through the ash of the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast.'

notes.title: Pack-Guar Cargo Tally: Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Caravan Master of Molag Mar
pages: Waybill recovered from a waxing-crate at Ancient Shipwreck (8584, 664 in the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast): six jars of refined scuttle, two bolts of boiled netch-leather, and one sealed brass tube addressed to the council clerk in Molag Mar across Azura's Coast.

notes.author: Council Archivist of Molag Mar
pages: Recorded in the House cadastre for Ancient Shipwreck (8584, 664 in Azura's Coast): all salvage, spore-rights, and ancestral niche-keys within Ancient Shipwreck remain subject to the custom of the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast and the magistrate's seal at Molag Mar.

notes.title: Armiger Courier Slip at Ancient Shipwreck
notes.author: Patrol-Signaler of Molag Mar
pages: Left in the bronze message-cylinder at Ancient Shipwreck (8584, 664): the ash-wind over Azura's Coast has shifted east; all riders bound for Molag Mar in the Pilgrim Bastions of Azura's Coast should check the ward-lanterns at Ancient Shipwreck before pressing on.

pages: On the fourteenth day of our circuit through the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles, we set our brass transit-rod at Punabi (survey grid 7294, 506 in the Ascadian Isles). The basalt and chitin foundations here show three distinct strata beneath the volcanic ash, and our Dunmer guide from Vivec City insisted on leaving a pinch of bonemeal at the threshold before sundown.

notes.title: House Watch Dispatch: Punabi
notes.author: Chancery of Vivec City
pages: To the watch-retainer posted at Punabi (7294, 506): by warrant of Archcanon Tholer Saryoni and Duke Vedam Dren in Vivec City, patrols along this sector of the Ascadian Isles are to inspect all night-caravans bearing unsealed ebony or flin crates. Any bearer carrying a red-wax Sixth House chime is to be detained and escorted to Vivec City at once.

notes.title: Factor's Private Missive from Punabi
notes.author: Factor-Clerk Llaren
pages: My dear colleague in Vivec City: the inventory stored at Punabi (grid 7294, 506 in the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles) remains untouched by the excise bailiffs. So long as the Ascadian Isles stays distracted by council rivalries, our pack-guars can move two dozen amphorae a week past Punabi without paying a single drake in tariff.

notes.title: Antiquarian Notes on Punabi
notes.author: Curator Mehra of the Hall of Wisdom
pages: Among the secondary sites of the Ascadian Isles, Punabi (situated at coordinates 7294, 506 within the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles) merits closer study by the Temple archivists. The lintel joints preserve tool-marks characteristic of early Velothi masonry, yet the lower drainage follows an older Dwemer alignment oriented toward Vivec City.

notes.title: Caravanner's Chalk-Warning at Punabi
notes.author: Silt-Strider Guide of Vivec City
pages: Travellers bound for Vivec City across the Ascadian Isles: do not tether your pack-guars at Punabi (7294, 506) when the ash-fog thickens at dusk. Three kagouti-hunters and a House outrider vanished near the outer stones of Punabi last fortnight, and the watch in the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles has not yet purged the interior.

notes.title: Rubbing from the Velothi Lintel at Punabi
notes.author: Temple Chronicler of Vivec City
pages: Transcribed from the ash-scoured lintel at Punabi (7294, 506 in the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles): 'Here stood the third hearth-watch of the the Ascadian Isles march, consecrated by the clan-elders on the high road to Vivec City. Let him who takes shelter within these stones keep the ancestor-coal lit and the threshold clean.'

notes.title: Tithe and Assay Roll of Punabi
notes.author: Factor-Steward of Vivec City
pages: Extracted from the district assessment book for Punabi (grid 7294, 506 in the Ascadian Isles): twelve bales of salted trama-root, four casks of sujamma, and eighteen ebony drakes remitted to the the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles wardens at Vivec City, with arrears noted since the latest ash-storms.

notes.title: Outrider's Night-Watch Report: Punabi
notes.author: Scout-Retainer of Vivec City
pages: Submitted to the guard-captain at Vivec City: at midnight we observed amber chitin-lanterns signaling from the upper ridge of Punabi (7294, 506 in the Ascadian Isles). Fresh guar-tracks lead from the postern toward the coast, matching the smuggling ring hunted across the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Ash-Slip Left at Punabi
notes.author: Wayfarer of the Seven Graces
pages: Tucked beneath a weathered cairn-stone at Punabi (7294, 506 in the Ascadian Isles): 'By courtesy, mercy, and valor, may the Three and our honoured ancestors watch over those who walk from Punabi to Vivec City through the ash of the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles.'

notes.title: Pack-Guar Cargo Tally: Punabi
notes.author: Caravan Master of Vivec City
pages: Waybill recovered from a waxing-crate at Punabi (7294, 506 in the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles): six jars of refined scuttle, two bolts of boiled netch-leather, and one sealed brass tube addressed to the council clerk in Vivec City across the Ascadian Isles.

notes.title: Boundary-Writ of Punabi
notes.author: Council Archivist of Vivec City
pages: Recorded in the House cadastre for Punabi (7294, 506 in the Ascadian Isles): all salvage, spore-rights, and ancestral niche-keys within Punabi remain subject to the custom of the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles and the magistrate's seal at Vivec City.

notes.title: Armiger Courier Slip at Punabi
notes.author: Patrol-Signaler of Vivec City
pages: Left in the bronze message-cylinder at Punabi (7294, 506): the ash-wind over the Ascadian Isles has shifted east; all riders bound for Vivec City in the Sacred Cantons of the Ascadian Isles should check the ward-lanterns at Punabi before pressing on.

black_book_sallow_regent.hook: Black Book Sallow Regent (landmark) stands at (4290, -3600) in Solstheim, where the weathered stone and chitin of the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim still bear the marks of Raven Rock's House and Temple history.
black_book_sallow_regent.rumour: Travellers in Raven Rock say anyone who searches Black Book Sallow Regent in Solstheim will find traces of the old Velothi wardens and recent smugglers' caches.

notes.title: Surveyor's Ash-Log at Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Vivec Geographical & Propylon Society
pages: On the fourteenth day of our circuit through the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim, we set our brass transit-rod at Black Book Sallow Regent (survey grid 4290, -3600 in Solstheim). The basalt and chitin foundations here show three distinct strata beneath the volcanic ash, and our Dunmer guide from Raven Rock insisted on leaving a pinch of bonemeal at the threshold before sundown.

notes.title: House Watch Dispatch: Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Chancery of Raven Rock
pages: To the watch-retainer posted at Black Book Sallow Regent (4290, -3600): by warrant of Councilor Lleril Morvayn and Shaman Storn Crag-Strider in Raven Rock, patrols along this sector of Solstheim are to inspect all night-caravans bearing unsealed ebony or flin crates. Any bearer carrying a red-wax Sixth House chime is to be detained and escorted to Raven Rock at once.

notes.title: Factor's Private Missive from Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Factor-Clerk Llaren
pages: My dear colleague in Raven Rock: the inventory stored at Black Book Sallow Regent (grid 4290, -3600 in the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim) remains untouched by the excise bailiffs. So long as Solstheim stays distracted by council rivalries, our pack-guars can move two dozen amphorae a week past Black Book Sallow Regent without paying a single drake in tariff.

notes.title: Antiquarian Notes on Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Curator Mehra of the Hall of Wisdom
pages: Among the secondary sites of Solstheim, Black Book Sallow Regent (situated at coordinates 4290, -3600 within the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim) merits closer study by the Temple archivists. The lintel joints preserve tool-marks characteristic of early Velothi masonry, yet the lower drainage follows an older Dwemer alignment oriented toward Raven Rock.

notes.title: Caravanner's Chalk-Warning at Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Silt-Strider Guide of Raven Rock
pages: Travellers bound for Raven Rock across Solstheim: do not tether your pack-guars at Black Book Sallow Regent (4290, -3600) when the ash-fog thickens at dusk. Three kagouti-hunters and a House outrider vanished near the outer stones of Black Book Sallow Regent last fortnight, and the watch in the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim has not yet purged the interior.

notes.title: Rubbing from the Velothi Lintel at Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Temple Chronicler of Raven Rock
pages: Transcribed from the ash-scoured lintel at Black Book Sallow Regent (4290, -3600 in the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim): 'Here stood the third hearth-watch of the Solstheim march, consecrated by the clan-elders on the high road to Raven Rock. Let him who takes shelter within these stones keep the ancestor-coal lit and the threshold clean.'

notes.title: Tithe and Assay Roll of Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Factor-Steward of Raven Rock
pages: Extracted from the district assessment book for Black Book Sallow Regent (grid 4290, -3600 in Solstheim): twelve bales of salted trama-root, four casks of sujamma, and eighteen ebony drakes remitted to the the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim wardens at Raven Rock, with arrears noted since the latest ash-storms.

notes.title: Outrider's Night-Watch Report: Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Scout-Retainer of Raven Rock
pages: Submitted to the guard-captain at Raven Rock: at midnight we observed amber chitin-lanterns signaling from the upper ridge of Black Book Sallow Regent (4290, -3600 in Solstheim). Fresh guar-tracks lead from the postern toward the coast, matching the smuggling ring hunted across the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Ash-Slip Left at Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Wayfarer of the Seven Graces
pages: Tucked beneath a weathered cairn-stone at Black Book Sallow Regent (4290, -3600 in Solstheim): 'By courtesy, mercy, and valor, may the Three and our honoured ancestors watch over those who walk from Black Book Sallow Regent to Raven Rock through the ash of the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim.'

notes.title: Pack-Guar Cargo Tally: Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Caravan Master of Raven Rock
pages: Waybill recovered from a waxing-crate at Black Book Sallow Regent (4290, -3600 in the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim): six jars of refined scuttle, two bolts of boiled netch-leather, and one sealed brass tube addressed to the council clerk in Raven Rock across Solstheim.

notes.title: Boundary-Writ of Black Book Sallow Regent
notes.author: Council Archivist of Raven Rock
pages: Recorded in the House cadastre for Black Book Sallow Regent (4290, -3600 in Solstheim): all salvage, spore-rights, and ancestral niche-keys within Black Book Sallow Regent remain subject to the custom of the Redoran & Skaal Marches of Solstheim and the magistrate's seal at Raven Rock.
